payload.blocks: ACE phase 3 and ASC phase 6: `fgos authority declare --kind component` refuses without --approved-by naming an answered owner question.
payload.headline: Approve declaring components agent-context-engine and agent-start-context in the authority model

parts.cause: The owner settled both in chat: ASC-D1 (discussion ds-2d55ty37zz, ASC is a tier-3 Rust crate) and ACE-D3 (discussion ds-e26zcar63f, ACE is its own component), with the order ACE then ASC (ACE-D2). The declare door requires that approval to exist as an answered question in the store.

options.does: Both components are declared with the rows of the two plans' Authority maps; ACE in its phase 3, ASC in its phase 6.
options.gain: ACE phase 3 and ASC phase 6 run without stopping for the owner.
options.harm: None beyond what ACE-D3 and ASC-D1 already settled.
options.label: Approve both as planned

options.does: Only agent-context-engine is declared now; ASC asks again before its phase 6.
options.gain: Keeps the ASC component open to change until ASC starts.
options.harm: ASC stops once more for the owner, months after ACE.
options.label: Approve ACE only

parts.recommendation: Approve both as planned: both decisions are already settled in the discussions, and this answer only records them for the declare door.

scope.allows: Declaring components agent-context-engine and agent-start-context, and their v1 contracts, with the rows named in the two plans' Authority maps.
scope.forbids: Any other component, and changing the owner of an existing decision kind (that needs --move with a plan naming the survivor).

parts.what: Two new components are about to be added to packages/component-authority/model: agent-context-engine (ACE: the single checked store of every fgOS rule, its when: key registry and its effective rule set) and agent-start-context (ASC: the only selector and composer of the text every fgOS-started agent receives). Their owners, contracts and overlaps are in the Authority map of plans 261125-1631 and 261122-1946.
